notes.1a: There were a high proportion of correct responses to this question.
notes.1b: This question was only answered well by the strongest candidates. There were many vague responses which included information on wind and wave turbines, solar panels or hydroelectric pumping stations.
notes.2a: Sections A and B were answered well by nearly all candidates. A small proportion of candidates indicated that the vessel was stationary at Section B. Only the better prepared candidates gained full credit indicating faster rate and higher speeds for Sections C and D.
notes.2b: Many candidates gave an incorrect response of 4 m, failing to take account of the time in minutes. In many cases credit for any correct working could not be awarded as candidates had not given an equation or shown their calculations. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics November 2017
notes.3ai: This question was answered well by stronger candidates.
notes.3aii: This was answered well by stronger candidates. Common errors were 45 and 4500.
notes.4a: This question was answered correctly by stronger candidates. A common incorrect response was “gravitational energy”.
notes.4b: There were many correct responses to this question. Incorrect responses usually indicated a point at the maximum displacement from the mid-point. There were a significant number of candidates who did not give a response to this question.
notes.4c: Stronger candidates were able to answer this question correctly. Common incorrect responses referred to gravitational force or resultant force.
notes.4d: This question proved challenging to many candidates but stronger candidates were able to answer correctly.
notes.5a: This was a challenging question for many candidates. Examples of insulators such as plastic and air were frequently seen and could not be credited.
notes.5b: Many candidates gained at least partial credit for their responses to this question recognising conduction, convection and evaporation as thermal energy transfer mechanisms. There was some evidence of candidates who had learned a response giving their answers in terms of air rather than a liquid.
notes.6a: There were many partially correct responses to this question. A common error was with the positioning of the angle of reflection. A small number of candidates failed to obtain credit for the last part stating that the incident ray was equal to the reflected ray rather than referring to the angles of incidence and reflection.
notes.6b: This was answered well by stronger candidates.
notes.6c: This question was answered well by many candidates. However few candidates were able to give a correct response for the focal length and 24 cm was a common wrong answer.
notes.7a: Purple and pink were common errors seen in answers to this question.
notes.7b: Stronger candidates were able to answer both parts of this question correctly.
notes.7c: Cancer was a common incorrect answer.
notes.7d: Many candidates gave a range of acceptable responses. Sound, longitudinal and transverse waves were common incorrect responses that could not be credited. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics November 2017
